newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast products ease as seller cut offers - Feb 13.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast products ease as seller cut offers - Feb 13.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot product values drifted down in subdued Thursday trade as sellers cut their offers with a weaker heating oil futures market, brokers said.
"Sellers want to get something sold and get short," a broker said.
Markets weakened as the NYMEX March heating oil settled down 0.93 cents a gallon to 59.92 cents, while crude and gasoline markets were up slightly, after trading lower in the morning.
Supply was seen adequate amid warmer temperature forecasts, traders said.
"As long as the Merc is down, we're going lower," one broker said.
Traders said 10,000 barrels of San Francisco CARB unleaded gasoline sold at 70 cents a gallon for February delivery, March barrels talked 71/72 cents.
CARB gasoline in L.A. was assessed 74/74.50, with offers about a half cent lower than Wednesday.
Los Angeles conventional ranged 70 to 70.50 cents about half a cent lower than late yesterday.
